sealed.statement: Every test in the census carries exactly one deterministically derived subsystem classification, sealed by a census-and-digest manifest whose --check mode fails when any test is unclassified, misclassified against its derivation, or lost; CI selection behaviour is unchanged by this Quest.
sealed.title: seal a subsystem classification over every test in the census

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The subsystem manifest census must equal the primary/resource census exactly. A test may never be dropped, silently defaulted, or double-counted by classification.

Every subsystem value must be derived from repository-declared state by a pure function of the test path and the declared owner boundaries, never from timing, filesystem contents outside the repository, or manual per-test edits that the deriver cannot reproduce.
This Quest adds classification only. No gate, manifest, or npm script may change which tests CI selects; the required check must run the same corpus before and after.

A test the deriver cannot classify must fail the --check mode by name. Assigning an unmatched test to a catch-all subsystem is forbidden, because silent under-classification is indistinguishable from correct classification.

note: Frame check: the implementation is right but the Quest FRAME is wrong. I sealed a statement about test classification without declaring that the work owns classification TOOLING, so the scope classifier reads runtime while the change touches package.json, docs/steering and solve/. The correct altitude for this work is workflow/tooling ownership, which the sealed statement cannot now acquire without a verifier-rejection finding that does not exist. Parking and re-declaring at the right altitude is cheaper and more honest than bending the amendment mechanism, and the guardrail caught a real declaration mistake rather than a false positive.

reason: Mis-scoped at declaration: the sealed statement did not declare ownership of test-classification TOOLING, so classifyQuestScope reads the Quest as runtime scope while the change legitimately touches workflow-owned surfaces (package.json, docs/steering/llm/tools-index.md, solve/). The changeRef gate correctly refused. statement-strengthen is unavailable because it requires a recorded verifier-rejection finding, and manufacturing one would turn that safety mechanism into ceremony. Parking for a correctly-scoped successor; the Stage-1 implementation is complete and proved.
